clue.text: She takes care of the minor issues

definitions.text: She takes care of the minor issues

parts.words: She takes care of the minor issues
parts.note: issues here means offspring, so the minor issues are small children, and the woman looking after them is a hired carer of the young

explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after a family's young children is exactly someone caring for little offspring.

clue.text: A piece of Ahab's in the drink

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A share of Captain Ahab's liquor, perhaps the grog of Moby-Dick's obsessive whaler.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinth is a strong green aniseed-flavoured spirit, so a kind of alcoholic liquor.

clue.text: A small spa resort in the Canary Islands

definitions.text: A small spa resort in the Canary Islands

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means put in order again, so the letters of the first three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A modest holiday town with health baths on one of Spain's Atlantic islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'resort' as 're-sort': the nine letters of A SMALL SPA are rearranged, while the whole clue describes the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Palmas, on Gran Canaria, is the main city and a holiday destination of Spain's Canary Islands.

clue.text: Overnight, this is an immediate hit

definitions.text: Overnight, this is an immediate hit

parts.words: Overnight, this is an immediate hit
parts.note: an instant success is often called an overnight something, and the clue asks for the noun that completes that phrase

explanation.definitionFit: A sensation is a person or thing causing great excitement and public interest, as an instant success does.

clue.text: Pick out the best

definitions.meaning: to pick out is to choose from a group
as an adjective, describing only the finest or most exclusive, as in a choice few

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means choose; as an adjective it describes an exclusive, top-quality group, as in a choice few.

clue.text: Famous person with autograph for Leo?

parts.note: a famous person is a celebrity or star
to autograph something is to sign it

explanation.surface: A celebrity scribbling a signature for a fan named Leo.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Leo as an example: it is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is one of the twelve zodiac divisions astrologers use, an example of the category.

clue.text: Brown top at first has strange fit

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: at first tells us to take only the opening letter of the word top

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A brown shirt sends someone into an odd fit of rage.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM meaning odd is old-fashioned British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit of temper is an outburst of rage, the kind a child throws.

clue.text: Have a target, but hitting the wrong one!

definitions.text: Have a target, but hitting the wrong one!

parts.note: to own something is to have it
a goal is an aim or target

explanation.surface: Aiming at a target but striking the wrong one.
explanation.walkthrough: In football this is putting the ball into your own team's net, which the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, scoring into your own net gives a point to the opposing side, an act against one's own interests.

clue.text: University doctor with kinky gear causes offence

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical degree, so a doctor

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters of gear are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A university medic in fetish clothing scandalises people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kinky' makes RAGE from GEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, so it means resentment at a slight.

clue.text: Making money and really wanting to go topless

indicators.note: losing its top means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: yearning is longing for something

explanation.surface: Someone eager to strip off and keen to be paid for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go topless' removes the opening Y of YEARNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning is gaining income through work, so the act of getting paid.

clue.text: Second drink leads to dotty painting

parts.note: a tipple is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Another drink makes an artist's work go a bit crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dotty' looks like it means mad, but here it literally means made of dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippling is the technique of painting or drawing with small dots.

clue.text: Where folk are taught about harem?

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
a harem is jokingly a room full of girls, a lass room

explanation.surface: Asking what lessons a sultan's harem might be given.
explanation.walkthrough: LASS is a British and Scottish word for a girl, so a harem is playfully a lass room.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils are taught in a schoolroom where lessons are given.

clue.text: It's like Aslan to harm one in row

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for row

parts.note: a row is a line

indicators.note: harm means damage, so the letters of one are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is like the Narnia lion to hurt someone standing in a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harm' turns ONE into EON, which goes 'in' LINE. Aslan is the lion in C S Lewis's Narnia books.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means lion-like, and Aslan is a lion.

clue.text: Destroy ultimate mangle

indicators.note: to mangle is to crush and twist out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A command to wreck the very last wringer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mangle' looks like a noun (an old laundry wringer) but works as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutilate is to damage severely, maim or ruin.

clue.text: It's good to stroll back

parts.note: to amble is to walk at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: Someone saying a walk back home would be nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a direction for the walk but is the definition: to back a horse is to bet on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a horse is to bet money on it, taking a risk.

clue.text: Adore Rome, so go here if flying

definitions.text: Adore Rome, so go here if flying

indicators.note: flying suggests something moving about, so the letters of the first two words are scattered

explanation.surface: A traveller who loves Rome is advised to come to the airfield if travelling by plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges ADORE ROME, and the whole clue describes where you depart by air.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerodrome is an airfield, a place where aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: This event is of school

indicators.note: to school is to drill or train, so the letters of the words before it are put through a new order

explanation.surface: Announcing that this event belongs to the school.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is of EVENT IS OF; Eton fives is a handball game played in a walled court, first played at Eton College, the English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: A handball game originating at Eton College, a famous English boarding school, and played between schools.

clue.text: Annie is foolish

indicators.note: foolish suggests letters behaving senselessly, so those of the first two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A remark that Annie is a silly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolish' rearranges ANNIE IS, while the whole clue says what Annie is.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means extremely stupid, literally like an ass.

clue.text: Good man to encourage producer of expensive eggs

parts.note: ST, saint, is the crossword shorthand for a good man
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A virtuous man cheering on a farmer whose eggs cost a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The eggs are caviar, the roe of this large fish, which is famously expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar is the salted roe of this large fish, among the costliest foods.

clue.text: Hate taking notes to exam

parts.note: D and E are musical notes
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: A student loathing having to take notes into an examination.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe intensely.

clue.text: Window cleaner's rubbish

definitions.meaning: the eye is the window of the soul, so this is a lotion for bathing the eye

explanation.definitionFit: A lotion for bathing sore eyes; also slang for nonsense meant to impress or mislead.

clue.text: The Sun quote me when upset — they make me vomit!

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: Someone sickened by being quoted in a tabloid newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when upset' reverses the whole run at once, since in a down clue upset reads as turned over. The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, and the reused 'me' is the setter's own touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Emetics are drugs or substances that induce vomiting.

clue.text: In oven, it's cooked

indicators.note: cooked means altered or rearranged, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the 's of it's supplies S

explanation.surface: A remark that something in the oven is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges IN OVEN with the S of 'it's'; the whole clue describes meat roasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is deer meat, which is roasted in the oven.

clue.text: Pig of an emperor

definitions.meaning: the boar who becomes dictator in George Orwell's Animal Farm
the French ruler Bonaparte, crowned in 1804

explanation.definitionFit: The tyrant boar in Orwell's Animal Farm takes his name from Bonaparte, the French ruler.

clue.text: Takes in a desperate man if terribly sick on first inspection

indicators.note: looking only at the first letter of each of the six words that come before

explanation.surface: A hospital accepts a desperate, very ill man once he has been examined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on first inspection' sounds like a doctor's examination but picks the initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital admits a patient when it receives them as an in-patient.

clue.text: Practised on transport when late going to director

parts.note: re means on or concerning
late means dead, and the vehicle carrying the dead is a funeral car

explanation.surface: Someone who runs through their lines on the bus when running behind for the director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' misleads as delayed; it means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise a performance before giving it.

clue.text: Dean's one for a drink

parts.note: Dean Martin was the American singer and actor
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Asking Dean to order one round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin and vermouth.

clue.text: Pit worker entertains king's seaman

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Pit worker entertains king's seaman': MINER around AR needs an A that no word gives (likely 'a king's' with the 'a' lost); no scan, and a search for the exact text found nothing

clue.text: Strange term Poe used for "in the time of"

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters of term Poe come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: An unusual word the writer Edgar Allan Poe used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges TERM POE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempore is Latin meaning in the time of, used in dates of reigns.

clue.text: Box mad horses

parts.note: a chest is a box
nuts is slang for mad

explanation.surface: Fighting crazy horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a verb (to fight) but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Chestnuts are horses with reddish-brown coats.
